newsitem.title: GUYANA: CRICKET-JOSHI TAKES FOUR WICKETS AS INDIA BEAT GUYANA.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-JOSHI TAKES FOUR WICKETS AS INDIA BEAT GUYANA.

text.p: Left-arm spinner Sunil Joshi took four wickets to lead India to a 91-win in their four-day match against Guyana on Monday, their first win since arriving in the Caribbean on tour in February.
Guyana, set a challenging 319 to win in 79 overs shortly before lunch on the final day, were bowled out for 227 in their second innings after India had declared on 277 for four.
The home side began badly, losing seven wickets for 108 runs, before being rescued by an eighth-wicket stand of 101 between Mahendra Nagamootoo and Neil Mcgarrell.
When they were removed, the home side's chances disappeared and Joshi finished the match when he dismissed Reon King to end with figures four for 74 off 24.5 overs.

Guyana were reduced to 22 for two by lunch, with fast bowler Abey Kuruvilla claiming opener Nicholas Degroot for nine and Rohan Sarjoo trapped leg before by fellow paceman Dodanarsiah Ganesh for three.

Ganesh then had Andre Percival out for five before Joshi and fellow spinner Noel David claimed four vital wickets between them. These included the scalp of captain Shivnarine Chanderpaul, who scored 176 in Guyana's first innings total of 300, for five.
Nagamootoo and Mcgarrell counter-attacked but their brave resistance ended when Nagamootoo was bowled on 47 by Joshi and Mcgarrell went leg before for 56 to Ganesh who finished with three for 25.

Then King edged a Joshi delivery to Navjot Sidhu at third slip to give India a confidence boosting win before their final test against the West Indies, which starts Thursday. India need to win the test to level the five-match.
Earlier, India, who drew previous tour games with Jamaica and Barbados, added 54 to their overnight score of 223 for three, losing only Saurav Ganguly, out for 81, before declaring.
